family.description: This entry represents a group of eukaryotic and archaeal proteins. Eukaryotic members include EMC3, a subunit of the ER membrane protein complex (EMC) required for protein folding [[cite:PUB00061987]], and TMCO1, a ER calcium load-activated calcium channel [[cite:PUB00081416]]. Archaeal members may function as insertases of the archaeal plasma membrane [[cite:PUB00086930]].
family.name: Integral membrane protein EMC3/TMCO1-like

Four minimal evidence ledgers and two open discussions retain TMCO1, archaeal and additional EMC coverage. Records baseline passed 8296 with zero drift; no completion or publication claim.

causal_graphs.context: Guna2018 Figure4C/D; matched empty versus EMC proteoliposomes. Separate native-RRL and isolated PURE-derived CaM-SQS preparations; protected C-terminal 3F4 fragment measured by autoradiography. Defined-complex assay uses 0.5 mM EGTA, 32 C for 20 min, then proteinase K and fragment IP; four experiments per graph, mean +/- SD.

evidence.explanation: Figure4C original image and main Results; empty/no-membrane, WT and EMC6-deficient microsome controls; native-RRL substrate.

edges.mechanism: Reconstituted assembled EMC increases the membrane-protected SQS reporter product relative to empty vesicles in Figure4C; the molecular catalyst is the complex, not an isolated Pfam domain.
edges.subject: rrl_emc

evidence.explanation: Figure4D original image, supplementary Methods pp5-6 and S18 orientation text; four experiments and active-orientation normalization, not EMC3-only sufficiency.

edges.mechanism: Purified assembled EMC supports SQS reporter insertion from an isolated CaM-bound substrate after EGTA-triggered release; increasing EMC at fixed lipid increases protected product over empty vesicles.
edges.subject: cam_emc

causal_graphs.family_mapping: The complex contains human EMC3, current reference Q9P0I2 v3, 261 aa, PF01956 5-191. The tag is on EMC5. Historical EMC3 sequence is not independently verified, and EMC3 is only one required complex component.
causal_graphs.limitations: Whole-complex assay sufficiency only. About one-third of reconstituted EMC is productively oriented. Fresh vesicles or once-frozen cholesterol-containing vesicles were used; specific lane assignment is not resolved. Figure4C timing is not explicitly separated from the general 15-min RRL protocol. Protected product is not native SQS catalytic activity; VAMP2 is a poorly inserted comparison substrate, not proof of universal specificity.

record.description: This entry represents a group of eukaryotic and archaeal proteins. Eukaryotic members include EMC3, a subunit of the ER membrane protein complex (EMC) required for protein folding [[cite:PUB00061987]], and TMCO1, a ER calcium load-activated calcium channel [[cite:PUB00081416]]. Archaeal members may function as insertases of the archaeal plasma membrane [[cite:PUB00086930]].

evidence.explanation: TMCO1 calcium-channel abstract inspected; full constructs, electrophysiology and cellular controls remain unreviewed.
Archaeal Ylp1 structural study is an imported citation lead, not yet an inspected insertion assay.

discussions.notes: Current TMCO1 Q9UM00 v2 is 239 aa; shorter Q9UM00-1 lacks canonical 1-51, but historical clones remain unverified. Selected 2020 and 2022 abundance/topogenesis effects are now retained. Review the inaccessible 2016 channel experiments, archaeal Ylp1, later native-client/holo-insertase work and original genetics. See evidence/PF01956/identity-and-boundaries.txt and tmco1-isoforms-and-constructs.txt. All earlier corpus follow-ups remain open.
discussions.prompt: Extend primary coverage to TMCO1, archaeal Ylp1 and remaining EMC3 systems without transferring mechanisms between them.
discussions.rationale: The retained experiments concern assembled human EMC, selected human/yeast EMC3 perturbations and selected human TMCO1/OPTI client-biogenesis contexts, not every member of this former DUF106 family.

evidence.explanation: Figure3 and S13 support variant-specific reporter effects; S9 is proximity evidence and the loop/thinning mechanism is a model.
Figures1/3 support yeast phenotypes; Hxt3 RNA decreases and gross complex assembly controls do not exhaust alternatives.
Figure4 and supplementary Methods support mixed-orientation EMC reconstitution; Figure4C timing, vesicle preparation assignment and trypsin protocol remain qualified.

discussions.notes: Verify variant plasmid sequences/junctions, endogenous-versus-exogenous stoichiometry and yeast alleles; inspect raw gels and unreviewed supplements. Pleiner supplement calls an amber codon UGA. Do not silently repair the source or turn crosslinking, membrane thinning or putative gating into observed sequential edges.
discussions.prompt: Resolve exact historical constructs and directly test the proposed insertion intermediates.
discussions.rationale: Reconstitution establishes whole-complex activity; cellular fluorescence, growth and localization do not identify each molecular step or isolated EMC3 sufficiency.

evidence.explanation: Abstract and postprint landing metadata inspected; CSU/publisher PDF access failed, so channel figures and D140 experiments remain unreviewed.
Figure5 and supplement1 support endogenous EAAT1 abundance effects; the proposed client-biogenesis explanation for calcium phenotypes is not direct experimental mediation.
Figures1/4 and Extended Data1/5 support partner abundance and separate topogenesis-sensitive endpoints, not isolated TMCO1 activity.

discussions.notes: Map exact historical sequences before residue-level edges. Resolve siRNA gating wording, stock/final culture concentrations, clone junctions and uninspected source data. Inspect substrate-driven recruitment perturbations and the accompanying structural work separately. No direct phenotype-to-phenotype chain or family-wide insertase/channel equivalence is inferred.
discussions.prompt: Distinguish TMCO1 channel claims from partner-dependent client biogenesis and resolve the historical constructs.
discussions.rationale: The 2020 and 2022 loss-of-function effects do not by themselves establish or disprove calcium permeation through TMCO1, and loss of TMCO1 also affects OPTI and translocon recruitment.
